title: People’s Mañanera August 14
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity’s Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available[here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Mexico Embraces You: Returning with Dignity  
** 271,000 Mexican nationals returned to the country and received more than
1.5 million services. These include food, health care, transportation, and
social well-being program benefits. President Claudia Sheinbaum noted that
Mexico welcomes them “with dignity, with respect, and with open arms.”

**Sovereignty: A Question of Defending the Homeland  
** Regarding the U.S. government’s decision to revoke visas for politically
engaged individuals, the President pointed to a possible political and
interventionist motive. Sheinbaum recalled that presidents Fox and Calderón
opened the doors to U.S. government agencies. “In Mexico, the Mexican people
decide,” she explained.

**Mexico Does Not Bow Down to Anyone  
** Sheinbaum defended a relationship with the United States free from
subordination and questioned those who seek foreign backing. “Why should we
lower our heads? Why should we bow down?,” she asked. The President affirmed
the country’s history of sovereignty, noting that “we are heirs to the best of
Mexico.”

**More Democracy, No Censorship  
** Sheinbaum defended codes of ethics, audience ombudsmen, and complaint
mechanisms proposed for the media. “What does that have to do with censorship?
Nothing,” she noted. The President contrasted these measures with the pressure
exerted on the media during the Fox and Calderón administrations and called
for transparency regarding manipulation in social media.

**Mexico Is Moving Toward Peace  
** August 13 was the safest day on record in recent history, with 20 homicides
registered nationwide. Sheinbaum highlighted the results of the security
strategy and noted that Mexico will present them at an international
conference in Argentina.

**Mexico: Things Are Going Well  
** It was emphasized that the economy will gain momentum in the second half of
the year, driven by new public works projects: “I told you the economy was
going to take off even more,” the President remarked.
